A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same pruning/distillation search and stage-aware inference framework. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial revisions and relocation of material.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark accuracy, perplexity, inference and pruning timings, cache-transmission measurements, ablations and robustness results in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains original benchmark, timing, ablation and robustness results and adds evaluations of stage-aware baseline variants in Table 2.

M1.justification: v4 removes the token-aware KV-cache pruning component described in v1 Section 3.2. The block-pruning/distillation search and stage adjustment remain, while v4 Section 4.2 introduces adaptations that use LLM-Pruner or ShortGPT to select decode removals and derive a prefill removal subset.

E1.justification: The separate evaluation on HPQA, 2WiKi, TQA, MuSiQue and SAMSum in v1 Appendix E disappears, removing a distinct QA/summarization benchmark suite. The main reasoning and knowledge benchmarks, instruction following, code generation and perplexity evaluations remain.

E2.justification: v4 Table 2 adds LLM-Pruner (Ours) and ShortGPT (Ours), explicitly evaluated PD-disaggregation adaptations. Conversely, the comparisons with LazyLLM, MInference and FlexPrefill disappear with the cache-pruning experiments. The original Table 1 comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Default calibration changes from 256 WikiText-2 examples to examples from PIQA and MMLU; distillation training changes from PIQA to PIQA plus MMLU. v4 also adds an approximately 50% pruning latency configuration and removes the cache-comparison and transmission protocols. These are reported setting changes; the PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v4 removes the cache-filtering ablation, cache-pruning sensitivity tests, cross-dataset cache-selection analysis and joint block/cache deployment analysis. Most block-focused analyses are retained or relocated, including iterative-search ablation, calibration robustness, quantization compatibility and qualitative cases. The restricted exhaustive-search comparison retains only five of its former nine benchmark columns.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental confidence intervals, error bars, significance tests, random seeds or repeated-run counts. The attention-head standard deviation used by v1's cache-scoring method is not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v4 adds adapted-baseline results and an approximately 50% pruning latency result of 151.89 ms. The 13.58% latency entry changes from 228.63 ms in v1 Table 2 to 236.63 ms in v4 Table 3; revised calibration and timing descriptions limit direct performance interpretation. All Table 1 numerical values remain unchanged, while the cache-related results disappear.

T1.justification: The substantive mathematical removal is the cache-scoring and layer-selection definitions in v1 Equations 27-29. The block-search mathematics and attention-perturbation bound remain equivalent; much of the derivation moves from the main text into v4 Appendices A-B.

C1.justification: v1 presents block pruning and token-aware cache pruning as complementary contributions, including explicit speedup and bandwidth-reduction claims. v4 narrows the central method to block pruning and stage sensitivity, removes the cache contribution and bandwidth claim, and adds a core claim of applicability to non-block pruning methods.

C2.justification: v4 interprets the adapted-baseline results as support for PD disaggregation as a general pruning principle and explains the cache-reuse rationale for the prefill/decode subset relationship in Appendix K. The earlier memory-management, dynamic-subgraph and MoE discussion disappears; the new Limitations section instead emphasizes unevaluated 70-billion-parameter models.

D1.justification: Core hardware, software, optimizer, learning-rate, batch-size and epoch details remain unchanged. v4 documents baseline adaptations and cache compatibility, revises training/calibration data descriptions, and omits construction-latency and search-iteration details. Appendix C still lists cache-pruning defaults despite removal of that method.

R1.justification: v4 removes the critique and supporting literature surrounding the KV-cache contribution, including attention sinks, H2O, MiniCache, SnapKV and the removed cache comparators. Positioning shifts toward stage-aware block pruning and compatibility with other pruning methods. The central PD-serving and block-pruning related work remains, with several general distillation and quantization citations added.

P1.justification: The introduction, contribution list and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Method subsections are reorganized, detailed derivations move into appendices, and unified evaluation, quantization and pruning overhead move into the main experiments. Hyperparameter analysis moves out of the main text. The title becomes PDTrim and the author list expands.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout. Figure 1 is extensively redrawn to show calibration, iterative search and cache reuse. Cache panels disappear from Figures 2-3, a new baseline table is added, the latency table gains a configuration, and the overhead table loses iteration columns. Numerous retained displays are relocated.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly strengthens the retained block-pruning argument: Table 2 provides more informative stage-aware comparisons, while Appendix K and the redrawn Figure 1 clarify cache compatibility. Most existing block results remain unchanged. These gains are tempered by unexplained data-description revisions alongside identical scores, residual cache-pruning parameters, and removal of the earlier memory-management limitation.
